problem: HER relieves sparse rewards but needs a goal representation that maps every state to an achieved goal; using the state space is redundant and uninformative, so HER is hard to apply to high-dimensional (pixel) 3D tasks.
motivation: Natural language is compact, flexible and compositional, so it can describe goals achieved in any state while generalizing across similar goals. Relabeling failed episodes with language descriptions from a teacher can turn sparse-reward multi-goal tasks into learnable ones.
key_idea: Extend HER by having a teacher give natural-language descriptions (positive achieved goals and negative unachieved goals) of each finished episode, and relabel the trajectory goal and reward with them in a language-conditioned DQN.
insight: Hindsight language advice is crucial: DQN without it fails on 7-object ViZDoom, compositional tasks and KGW. Language goal representations (GRU/InferLite) matter on compositional tasks (one-hot 24% vs GRU 97%) and allow zero-shot generalization to unseen instructions; a pre-trained sentence embedding gives partial robustness to synonyms. Only 1% of frames with advice recovers most performance (MT 0.73 vs 0.80 for GRU).
method: Teacher T(s): produces natural-language description of goal achieved in terminal state (from emulator state); multiple teachers can give different descriptions

Hindsight relabeling: each episode is stored in the replay buffer with original goal and additionally with each advice goal g' and its reward (1 for achieved, 0 for unachieved/discouraging), using DQN (Double DQN, n-step)
Positive and negative advice: a 'knowledgeable' teacher (describes achieved goals, including undesirable ones) plus a 'discouraging' teacher (describes unachieved desired goals with reward 0)
Language encoders: GRU over one-hot words (hidden 256), frozen pre-trained InferLite sentence embedding projected to 256, and a one-hot goal ID baseline
Gated-attention architecture (Chaplot et al.): the language vector becomes a sigmoid attention gating conv feature maps, followed by an LSTM and Q-value output
Compositional tasks: 'A and B' / 'A or B' goals, with HUD showing reached objects in ViZDoom

setting.backbone: DQN (Double DQN) with gated-attention CNN + GRU/InferLite language encoder + LSTM (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: RL from scratch in the simulator with 56 training instructions (15 held-out for ZSL); hindsight advice generated by scripted teachers; up to ~16M frames
setting.observation: first-person RGB image 3x300x168 (ViZDoom); global grid view (KrazyGrid World); plus language instruction
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: turn left, turn right, move forward (ViZDoom); up/down/left/right (+flag) in KGW
setting.privileged: teacher uses ground-truth emulator state to generate hindsight advice during training (not at test time)

numbers.extra: 16M frames; MT = train instructions, ZSL = held-out instructions; averaged over 2 seeds
MT and ZSL success over 100 episodes, 2 seeds
numbers.evidence: Table 1: ACTRCE (GRU) Single (7 objects) MT 0.80±0.06, ZSL 0.76±0.03

numbers.extra: one word replaced by a synonym (unseen lexicon)

numbers_note: Not a standard navigation benchmark; custom ViZDoom/KGW environments. KGW results only in figures (~80% SR).
results: ACTRCE reaches 80% MT/76% ZSL on 7-object ViZDoom where DQN gets 8%/6.5%, and 97% on compositional tasks (one-hot 24%, DQN ~11%). On 5-object hard mode it beats DQN (0.69 vs 0.4 at 8M frames) and is about an order of magnitude more sample-efficient than A3C.
limitations: Requires a teacher (here scripted from emulator states) to generate language descriptions; real human advice is not tested
Only simple, small synthetic environments with templated instructions and few seeds (2); not real scenes or realistic language
